scope: Pacify-X runtime, canonical memory, activity lifecycle, Knowledge Core, graph, Agent Builder, dashboard, sidebar protocol, VSIX identity, release packaging, and certification evidence

completion_claim.reason: Source repairs are complete and focused/section validation is green; exact installed-artifact, full-profile certification, and independent acceptance remain required.

findings.finding: The installed VS Code host is Pacify-X 0.5.5 while repaired repository source declares 0.6.8.
findings.acceptance: Install and smoke-test one newly versioned VSIX whose recorded digest matches the certified artifact.

findings.finding: The previous 0.6.4 VSIX did not match the final 0.6.4 source, so one semantic version identified multiple byte sets.
findings.acceptance: Bump the extension version, build once, and bind source, package, VSIX, and installed-host identities.

findings.finding: Completion and certification were false; ten group receipts were stale and 39 prior findings awaited verification.
findings.acceptance: All required group and section receipts are current, exactly one full profile passes, validate passes, and open findings reach zero.

findings.finding: Canonical workspace memory is detached because no valid workspace root and initialized workspace are selected.
findings.acceptance: Guided setup can initialize/select a canonical workspace and establish a current lease without substituting portable records.

findings.finding: Canonical memory browse and dashboard readiness could treat expired active-session projections as live leases.
findings.acceptance: All retrieval and readiness paths fail closed on invalid or expired leases and expose renewal/reacquisition state.

findings.finding: Seven orphan executable operations remained projected as active history with no terminal reconciliation evidence.
findings.acceptance: Stale operations are separated from live work and can be append-only reconciled with deterministic terminal receipts.

findings.finding: Historical actor sessions polluted current presence and lacked explicit live, stale, and history separation.
findings.acceptance: Current presence is lease/heartbeat-derived; historical actors remain inspectable without appearing live.

findings.finding: Knowledge Graph exposed only a bounded neighborhood while presenting it as the full map.
findings.acceptance: A complete aggregate overview reports full denominators and supports drill-down into bounded neighborhoods.

findings.finding: Depth-six graph placement overlapped incoming and contextual nodes.
findings.acceptance: Deterministic layout has unique, bounded positions and adequate node spacing at supported limits.

findings.finding: The graph lacked semantic clustering, level-of-detail navigation, and scalable overview rendering.
findings.acceptance: Overview, cluster, and neighborhood levels are distinct and preserve totals, filters, selection, and provenance.

findings.finding: Edge labels and secondary node text were too low-contrast for reliable inspection.
findings.acceptance: Graph labels meet the dashboard contrast/readability gate at supported zoom and viewport sizes.

findings.finding: Knowledge Core UI did not operate the existing browse/propose/verify/approve/promote/reject/rollback/recover controller.
findings.acceptance: The UI exposes real controller state and routes each admitted lifecycle action through host approval and receipts.

findings.finding: Advanced maintenance contradicted the backend by disabling rebuild and promotion even when admitted routes were available.
findings.acceptance: Availability, prerequisites, denial reasons, and action labels are projected from canonical controller data.

findings.finding: Knowledge lifecycle content clipped at common 1050-1208px widths without body overflow detection.
findings.acceptance: No local panel overflow or clipped lifecycle content at every certified viewport.

findings.finding: Dashboard connected/ready labels did not detect installed-host, source, asset protocol, or artifact identity splits.
findings.acceptance: A visible identity block and mismatch banner bind host version, source version, asset protocol, and artifact digest; mismatch cannot appear green.

findings.finding: Punch-card projections overstated closure while independent verification and live-host proof remained pending.
findings.acceptance: Completion projection counts every registry and refuses closure on stale or verification-pending evidence.

findings.finding: Visual evidence was explicitly synthetic and responsive tests omitted Knowledge Core local-overflow geometry.
findings.acceptance: Exact-installed-host evidence is labeled honestly and automated geometry covers every primary surface and local scroll container.

findings.finding: sidebar-inbound-message-invalid:type:invalid_union had no closed root-cause record or stale-asset/schema discrimination.
findings.acceptance: Diagnostics classify schema, asset, and unknown-type mismatches without content leakage and regression tests reproduce each case.

findings.finding: Agent Studio exposed PX's governed AgentSpec, grants, bindings, tests, and policies as a raw JSON textarea with no structured composition, live validation, domain isolation, or canonical round trip.
findings.acceptance: A keyboard-accessible PX-native visual Agent Builder represents every canonical field, validates conservatively, prevents standard/enterprise bleed, round-trips canonical JSON, and passes interaction plus backend contract gates.

findings.finding: The receipt-derived completion_status.json projection was hashed into static artifact reachability, so advancing certification receipts made the stored completion projection stale while refreshing it invalidated the receipts it summarized.
findings.acceptance: Live receipt projections are excluded from static artifact reachability, the exclusion has a regression test, completion status can refresh without changing static group inputs, and all affected receipts pass on the stable graph.

findings.finding: The canonical artifact-manifest generator ignored setuptools package-data declarations, so the wheel and source distribution contained runtime/studio_operations.json while exact artifact verification classified it as undeclared.
findings.acceptance: Artifact manifests generically project declared package data into wheel and source-distribution paths, reject missing patterns, and the built artifacts pass exact manifest verification.

findings.finding: The exact installed VSIX rendered 24 graph nodes and 23 edges, but Electron reported zero layout rectangles for both nested controls and SVG foreignObject frames, making DOM-rectangle visibility acknowledgement falsely report zero visible nodes.
findings.acceptance: Graph acknowledgement projects canonical node coordinates through the live pan/zoom transform and canvas bounds, browser tests require a nonzero geometry message, and one immutable newly versioned VSIX passes exact installed-host certification.

findings.finding: The retained exact-installed-host receipt copied the canonical dashboard source object verbatim and persisted the local engine root as an absolute machine path, invalidating portable evidence and cascading into release and structural audits.
findings.acceptance: The installed-host verifier uses the absolute engine root only for live comparison, sanitizes the retained receipt to an explicit connected-root token, and portability plus release/structural gates pass with zero unresolved external locators.
